en_title: The Loneliness of Sonia and Sunny: A Love Story With Other Lives Around It
zh_title: 《索尼娅与桑尼的孤独》：他们遇见彼此以前，已经有太多人替他们安排人生
en_deck: A family calls America to ask why a well-fed, successful student is lonely. Kiran Desai's opening makes room for a romance—and for the people a romance cannot leave behind.
zh_deck: 功课顺利，食堂丰盛，家人仍想不通Sonia为什么孤独。一场跨越印度与美国的爱情，先从关心与理解之间的距离开始。
en_notice: Introduces the opening and the couple's circumstances around their first meeting, without revealing major relationship turns or the ending. Includes emotional control, racial prejudice, and family conflict. Linked interviews and reviews discuss more of the novel.
zh_notice: 涉及情感控制、种族偏见与家庭冲突。介绍开篇及主要人物相识前后的基本处境，不透露重要关系转折与结局。中文书名为参考译名，人名保留原文。所链访谈及评论可能透露更多情节。
en_body:
Sonia's family has heard that she keeps crying on the telephone. She is studying in America, doing well academically, surrounded by opportunities that ought to make her happy. Her grandfather and aunt call the dormitory to investigate. How are her studies? What does she eat?

The account of the dining hall becomes increasingly lavish. There are dishes from different countries and an abundance of desserts. To the people asking the questions, this makes her unhappiness more mysterious. How can someone with so much be lonely?

The [opening sample of Kiran Desai's *The Loneliness of Sonia and Sunny*](https://cdn.penguin.co.uk/dam-assets/books/9780241770825/9780241770825-sample.pdf) finds comedy inside an earnest attempt to help. The relatives reach for familiar measures of a good life. Each answer seems to remove a possible cause of distress, yet Sonia remains distressed. Their concern is real; so is their inability to imagine the condition she is trying to describe.

It is an inviting beginning for a love story. Before meeting its couple together, we encounter the distance between being cared about and being understood. A romance will have plenty to enter besides an empty space waiting for another person.

## Two journeys to America

The novel's central young people have both left India, but departure has not given them equivalent lives. Sonia is studying in Vermont and wants to write fiction. Sunny is in New York, trying to establish himself as a journalist. Their families can regard these moves as progress while the people making them feel far less certain.

For Sonia, the wish to become a writer is bound up with the difficulty of finding a voice. An older artist offers intimacy and inspiration, then becomes a damaging presence. The situation places several kinds of authority in one relationship: lover, guide, and judge of artistic worth.

That combination can make approval unusually powerful. Someone who hopes to learn from another person's way of seeing may begin to depend on it when looking at herself. The premise is interesting because an apparently expansive life in the arts can contain a very narrow field of permission.

Sunny is seeking distance from his mother's control. He has an American girlfriend, but an intimate relationship does not settle the question of belonging. His professional ambition also involves other people's expectations about what he can explain and who he is supposed to be.

[Jane Wallace, reviewing the novel for Asian Review of Books](https://asianreviewofbooks.com/the-loneliness-of-sonia-and-sunny-by-kiran-desai/), draws attention to his position as a journalist describing India for Western media. The work brings him up against established ways of presenting the country. Being able to tell a story is not the same as being free to choose its frame.

The novel is set mainly in the late 1990s and early 2000s. Migration, racial assumptions, and family expectations supply specific pressures rather than a generic atmosphere of displacement. Each young person has acquired opportunities without necessarily acquiring the freedom imagined by those at home.

Returning to India cannot simply reverse these journeys. Sonia and Sunny bring their unsettled lives with them.

## A meeting with other people behind it

The [publisher's account of their first meeting](https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/212138/the-loneliness-of-sonia-and-sunny-by-kiran-desai/) places Sonia and Sunny on an overnight train in India. They are attracted to one another, with an awkward complication: their grandparents have already tried to bring them together. The earlier attempt at matchmaking made them resistant.

Now an actual person is in front of each of them. Refusing an arrangement does not oblige someone to dislike the person proposed. The encounter promises the pleasures of romantic uncertainty without reducing the choice to obedience or rebellion.

Their families also have lives that cannot be conveniently cleared from the scene. Sunny's mother, Babita, wants influence over her son and fears being left behind. Her interference may be suffocating while her fear remains intelligible. Understanding it need not make him responsible for arranging his entire future around it.

Around the central pair are parents, grandparents, aunts, and people whose work sustains the households. Some have travelled far; others have remained in familiar surroundings. Being surrounded by relatives does not ensure an equal opportunity to speak, or a listener willing to hear something unfamiliar.

The opening telephone call has already prepared us for this larger company. Food and achievement are supposed to make Sonia's experience understandable. The exchange also reveals something about the people using those measures. The caller and the person called can occupy different kinds of loneliness.

That gives the family novel a richer prospect than an argument between traditional parents and modern children. Young people can want independence and familiar approval at the same time. They may recognize their parents' limitations while carrying some of the same expectations into their own relationships.

## Room for a life of one's own

In her [Booker Prize interview](https://thebookerprizes.com/the-booker-library/features/kiran-desai-interview), Desai describes wanting a contemporary romance that retained an older kind of beauty. Her characters encounter possibilities across countries and communities. Why this person rather than someone else? Why stay here when life might continue elsewhere?

Such questions can make choice feel less secure as its range expands. The author explains that moving across generations and places also enlarged her understanding of loneliness. Romantic longing became one part of a broader interest in divisions of class, race, history, and national belonging.

Sonia's desire to write adds another complication. Solitude may be painful, but time alone can also be necessary for the work she wants to do. A companion cannot write the book for her or remove every difficulty involved in becoming its author.

Desai tells [Elaine Szewczyk in Publishers Weekly](https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/authors/profiles/article/98271-kiran-desai-s-labor-of-love.html) that loneliness can be a gift to an artist. This is an observation about her own creative experience, not a prescription for how Sonia ought to live. It nevertheless offers a useful distinction: love need not eliminate every form of aloneness.

Nor must the prospective lovers first become perfectly considerate people. In her [Chicago Review of Books assessment](https://chireviewofbooks.com/2025/09/24/to-be-alone-is-to-be-understood-a-review-of-the-loneliness-of-sonia-and-sunny/), Malavika Praseed notes how Sonia's hurt coexists with behaviour that makes accepting help difficult. Sympathy for what happened to someone can survive an honest account of how that person treats others.

The attraction here lies in two unfinished lives meeting. They might make one another's world larger without becoming the answer to everything within it.

## The invitation of a long book

At nearly seven hundred pages, this is a substantial commitment. The interviews and reviews suggest that its length does more than postpone the lovers' arrival at an answer. The narrative turns outward toward other households, working lives, cities, art, and unsettling experiences.

Whether those excursions remain rewarding is where the published assessments diverge. Wallace admires Desai's movement between comedy and tragedy, the lyrical and the coarse. She finds value in reaching the central story through many surrounding ones.

Praseed praises the novel's scale and social insight but finds some supporting characters' recurring mannerisms tiring. She distinguishes these reservations from a simple objection to slowness: the descriptions and wider scope can also be among the book's strengths.

Those are judgments of the complete novel. The excerpt offers a smaller, practical test. Does the family's conversation make you want to hear more from these people, even when they are getting things wrong? Does a discussion of dinner become interesting for what it reveals about the speakers?

Desai's humour, in those early pages, makes concern and incomprehension audible together. The relatives are not merely obstacles waiting for Sonia's real life to begin. They are already living lives of their own, with pleasures, restrictions, and desires she may not fully see.

The title naturally directs us toward Sonia and Sunny. The telephone suggests why we might also want to stay with the people around them. Being placed beside somebody else's love story does not make a person's own day a digression.
zh_body:
Sonia在美国读大学，家人听说她近来总在电话里哭。祖父和姑姑打到宿舍，先问功课，再问食堂吃些什么。她学业顺利，食堂里有各国菜式与甜点。听起来，生活的条件实在不坏，那么她为什么还会孤独？

这是[出版社公开试读](https://cdn.penguin.co.uk/dam-assets/books/9780241770825/9780241770825-sample.pdf)中，小说开篇的一通电话。电话另一端的家人并非全不关心她，他们在用自己熟悉的方法寻找问题。只是越问，越不能明白，为什么一个已经得到许多机会的人，仍然可以如此难过。

《索尼娅与桑尼的孤独》从这种错位进入爱情。它会让两个年轻人相遇，却先使我们知道，找到一个恋人以前，他们已经背着各自的生活。

## 他们都去了美国，却没有抵达同一种未来

故事主要发生在二十世纪九十年代后期至新世纪初，来往于印度与美国，也会延伸到其他地方。Sonia想写小说，在佛蒙特州完成学业；Sunny则在纽约试着做一名记者。两人的出国都很容易被家人理解为向前走了一步。

可是，向前走，并不一定意味着知道自己应该走向哪里。

对Sonia而言，写作不是一项只要成绩够好就能顺利完成的安排。她想成为作家，却也需要在陌生的生活里辨认自己的声音。此时，一位年长艺术家进入她的生命：她原本从他那里寻找亲密与启发，关系却逐渐成为伤害。

这条线使小说里的艺术不只是一种美好的志向。当一个人同时成为恋人、艺术上的引路人和评价者，他的赞许便可能占据过大的位置。年轻作者以为自己正在学习看世界，也可能渐渐只能通过对方的眼睛看自己。

Sunny的问题则有另一种形状。他想离开母亲的支配，也已经在美国建立亲密关系，但纽约不会因此变成一个无需解释自己的地方。职业上的愿望，与他怎样被周围人看待，并不是同一件事。

他与美国女友共同生活，但拥有亲密关系，并没有使归属的问题自动消失。他想摆脱家人规定的生活，也必须面对另一个社会加在自己身上的期待。

[Jane Wallace在Asian Review of Books的评论](https://asianreviewofbooks.com/the-loneliness-of-sonia-and-sunny-by-kiran-desai/)中，特别注意到Sunny作为记者的位置：他试图向西方媒体讲述印度，也必须面对新闻叙述已经预设的眼光。这使他的职业处境与私人生活接在一起。一个人能够说话，不等于他能够不受限制地决定从哪里说起。

因此，两人回到印度时，并不是已经完成自我探索的现代青年。他们带回了一些见识，也带回许多尚未解决的困难。回乡并不会自动使这些困难消失。

## 一次相遇，身后跟着两个家庭

[出版社介绍](https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/212138/the-loneliness-of-sonia-and-sunny-by-kiran-desai/)给出的相遇，发生在印度的一列夜车上。Sonia与Sunny相见，受到彼此吸引，却也有些尴尬：原来长辈此前就试图撮合他们。这件事曾经让两人抗拒，如今真正面对面，相处又不完全按原先的想法进行。

这个起点很适合写一部热闹的爱情小说。两个人都以为自己不愿接受安排，却不能因为长辈曾经安排过，就坚持对眼前的人毫无兴趣。拒绝被替自己作决定，与拒绝所有恰好符合他人期待的选择，并不是一回事。

但他们也不能假装，只要相爱，家人就会退出故事。Sunny的母亲Babita格外难以被留在背景里。她想控制儿子的生活，同时也害怕被儿子留下。她的干涉既令人窒息，又不只是一个阻碍爱情的功能。

Sonia与Sunny的家里还有祖辈、父母、姑辈，以及长期在家庭中做事的人。这个庞大的人物群并不只是提供文化背景，也使书名里的孤独出现不同的面貌。有的人远在国外，有的人从未离开家，周围一直有人，仍然很难找到能够说话的位置。

从这个角度看，爱情不是两位主角独占的一条通道。他们可能从家人的婚姻里继承期待，也继承恐惧；可能急于证明自己与上一代不同，却在相处时发现，熟悉的语气仍会从自己嘴里出来。

小说因而有机会写到比“自由恋爱还是家庭安排”更细的地方。我们一方面不愿被规定，一方面又希望自己的选择得到熟悉的人认可。两种愿望常常一起存在，未必能够先解决其中一种，再安心去爱。

## 孤独并不总是等着爱情来治好

Desai在[布克奖网站的访谈](https://thebookerprizes.com/the-booker-library/features/kiran-desai-interview)中说，她想写一段属于当代的恋爱：两个人会在不同国家相遇、分开，身边不断出现其他生活的可能。为什么是这个人，而不是另一个？为什么留在这里，而不是去别处？选择越多，答案未必越稳。

对于Sonia，独处还有写作的意义。她不只是希望摆脱孤独，也希望能成为一个拥有自己工作的作家。这两种需要未必随时一致。有人陪伴很好，但陪伴不能替她完成写作，更不能使她不再需要自己的时间。

Desai在[Publishers Weekly的访谈](https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/authors/profiles/article/98271-kiran-desai-s-labor-of-love.html)中，把艺术家的孤独看作一种可能的馈赠。这是作者谈创作经验，不能简单当作人物命运的答案，却能帮助我们理解：小说为什么没有把一切独处都放在需要修复的一边。

同样，亲密也不等于把彼此的缺陷都照顾妥当。Sonia受过伤，仍然可能让靠近她的人感到困难；Sunny想获得理解，也可能没有弄清自己对别人的要求。小说不需要他们先成为理想伴侣，才让爱情发生。

这里最值得保留的，或许就是两个人各自尚未完成的部分。另一个人可以使生活变得不同，却未必能够替自己回答所有问题。希望被爱，与把全部答案交给爱，仍然隔着很长一段距离。

## 愿不愿意跟着这本书多走一些路

《索尼娅与桑尼的孤独》接近七百页。从访谈与评论呈现的范围看，它的长篇幅并不只用于延宕恋人相聚，也不断往周围看：从家庭到城市，从工作到艺术，也容纳诡异的感受、讽刺与喜剧。

这种伸展，正是评论意见分开的地方。Wallace喜欢作品在诗意、粗粝、喜剧与悲剧之间转换的能力，认为旁支故事使我们从多个方向接近中心。[Malavika Praseed在Chicago Review of Books的评论](https://chireviewofbooks.com/2025/09/24/to-be-alone-is-to-be-understood-a-review-of-the-loneliness-of-sonia-and-sunny/)中，则一面肯定它的规模和社会观察，一面认为部分配角反复占据篇幅，读久了会疲倦。

后者也指出，节奏慢不必然是缺点；问题在于，读者能否从这些绕行中不断获得东西。这比笼统地把它称作“宏大”更有助于判断：如果你喜欢在人物很多、关系纠缠的小说里慢慢住下来，它有足够宽阔的空间；若期待清晰紧凑的爱情推进，则可能需要调整预期。

从公开试读看，Desai很会把沉重的问题藏进热闹的谈话。家人越认真寻找解决办法，读者有时越想笑，也越能感到他们彼此之间的距离。幽默没有使这些人变得无足轻重，反而让关心与误解可以同时出现在一句话里。

这也是继续读下去的理由。Sonia与Sunny当然使人好奇：他们会怎样靠近，又会怎样妨碍彼此？但书里不只有他们需要一个属于自己的生活。读得稍久，也许某位原先令人嫌烦的亲属，会开始使我们想多听他说一点。

毕竟，一个人被放在爱情故事的旁边，并不意味着他自己的日子就是旁枝。
